title: Orosius and the Recognitions: pagans own one God with many ministers
source_text: LXXIV. Sic refert Orosius Paganos fateri solitos non se plures Deos sequi, sed sub uno Deo Magno plures Ministros venerari. Sic etiam vetus Recognitionum scriptor eosdem Paganos dicentes introducit, Unum esse & nos dicimus Deum qui est omnium Dominus. Sed & isti Dii sunt. Sicut enim unus est Caesar, & habet sub se multos judices, verbi gratia Praefectos, Consules, Tribunos, & caeteras Potestates; simili arbitramur modo, cum unus sit omnium Deus, etiam istos ad similitudinem earum, quas diximus Potestatum, ordinatos esse in hoc mundo Deos, illi quidem majori subjectos, nos tamen & quae in hoc mundo sunt dispensantes. Oros. histor. lib. 6. init. Clem. Recogn. lib. 5.
pass_a_gloss: Thus Orosius reports that the Pagans were accustomed to confess that they did not follow many Gods, but under one great God venerated many Ministers. Thus also the old writer of the Recognitions introduces the same Pagans saying: We too say that there is one God who is Lord of all. But these also are Gods. For as there is one Caesar, and he has under him many judges, for example Prefects, Consuls, Tribunes and the other Powers; in a similar way we think, since there is one God of all, that these also, after the likeness of those Powers which we named, have been ordained Gods in this world, subject indeed to that greater one, yet dispensing us and the things which are in this world. Orosius, Histories book 6 beginning; Clement, Recognitions book 5.
pass_b_english: So Orosius reports that the pagans used to say they did not follow many gods, but venerated many servants under one great God.

So too the old author of the Recognitions brings in the same pagans saying: "We also say that there is one God, who is Lord of all. But these too are gods. For just as there is one Caesar, who has many judges under him, such as prefects, consuls, tribunes and the other authorities, in the same way we think that, since there is one God of all, these too have been appointed gods in this world on the pattern of the authorities we have named. They are subject to the greater one, but they govern us and all that is in this world." (Orosius, Histories, book 6, beginning; Clement, Recognitions, book 5.)

lemmas.latin: nos tamen & quae in hoc mundo sunt dispensantes
lemmas.gloss: yet administering us and the things in this world

lemmas.latin: ordinatos esse in hoc mundo Deos
lemmas.gloss: to have been appointed gods in this world

choices.why: Dispensare is to manage or administer; the pagans make the lesser gods stewards of the world under the supreme God.
